cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Dance Works
cards.back: Evaluation means making informed judgements about how effectively a dance communicates its intention

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Dance Works
cards.back: Effective evaluation requires clear criteria — such as how well movement, structure and design serve the intention

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Dance Works
cards.back: Evaluation builds on description and analysis — you must first understand what happens and how it works

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Dance Works
cards.back: A judgement must always be supported with specific evidence from the dance

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Dance Works
cards.back: You can evaluate a dance as highly effective, partially effective or ineffective, but must explain why

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Dance Works
cards.back: Evaluation considers whether the choreographic choices successfully communicate meaning to the audience

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Dance Works
cards.back: When evaluating, consider the whole work as well as specific moments or sections

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Dance Works
cards.back: The effectiveness of a dance depends on how well action, dynamic, spatial and relationship content work together

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Dance Works
cards.back: Design elements — costume, lighting, set and aural setting — also contribute to overall effectiveness

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Dance Works
cards.back: AQA marks evaluation that shows independent thinking and personal response supported by evidence

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Dance Works
cards.back: Evaluating your own choreography requires honesty about strengths and weaknesses with specific examples

cards.front: Recall a key point about Evaluating Dance Works
cards.back: Strong evaluation uses comparative language: 'more effective because…', 'less successful as…'

cards.front: What should you know about gcse dance exam tips — evaluating dance works?
cards.back: 1. For Evaluating Dance Works questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Evaluating Dance Works 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
Explain how to evaluate a dance work effectively. Describe the process and give an example of evaluating a specific choreographic feature. [6 marks]
